meta.title: Who Watches Whom: reading for a budgeted overseer
meta.author: Ameer Alhashemi

slides.title: Who Watches Whom
slides.subtitle: What I read for a budgeted overseer in sequential social dilemmas

slides.title: What I read for

items.head: The question
items.text: Can an overseer that checks only k of N learning agents per step keep cooperation going in a sequential social dilemma (SocialJax Harvest first)?

items.head: What it must decide
items.text: Whom to check each step, and what consequence to apply to agents it catches over-harvesting.

items.head: The test
items.text: Agents that learn to evade it: the overseer has to work against learners, not fixed or scripted agents.

items.head: What I checked in each paper
items.text: Is there an intervener? Does it see every agent? Does it choose whom to check? Do agents adapt to it?

slides.notes: Seven papers read properly and filled into the literature matrix; each answers these four checks.

slides.title: Every intervener so far sees everyone
slides.caption: Seven papers scored on the checks that define the gap. "Partly" in the first column means matrix games, a not-quite dilemma, or a shared team reward.
slides.takeaway: No paper combines learning agents in a dilemma with a budgeted overseer that chooses whom to check against agents that adapt.
slides.notes: Baumann's planner, Gasztowtt's LLM tax-setter and Sun's detector all see every agent. Casheekar is the only one with a budget, but its audit plan is fixed and agents never evade it.

slides.title: Four kinds of paper

cards.label: Setting
cards.head: The setting
cards.text: Leibo 2017, SocialJax, OpenSocialJax: sequential social dilemmas and fast benchmarks. No intervener at all.

cards.label: Sees all
cards.head: Planners that see all
cards.text: Baumann 2020 and Gasztowtt 2024: a planner or LLM sets rewards or taxes using every agent's actions or harvest.

cards.label: Sees all
cards.head: No police, still a watcher
cards.text: Sun 2019: peers boycott defectors, but a global detector reads every agent's reward history.

cards.label: Budget
cards.head: A budget, but fixed
cards.text: Casheekar 2026: random audits on a budget, but a team reward, a plan fixed in advance, and no evasion.

slides.takeaway: The pieces exist separately; nobody has put a budgeted, choosing overseer against adaptive learners in an SSD.

slides.title: The two closest papers
slides.caption: Casheekar is the only paper with a budgeted intervener; Gasztowtt is the only one with an LLM overseer in Harvest.
slides.takeaway: Neither chooses whom to check from what it sees, and in neither do agents learn to evade it.
slides.notes: Casheekar: certificate-built audit plan 57.4% unsafe completion vs 99.6% for coalition audits, same budget. Gasztowtt: GPT-4o mini converges in 36k steps on Harvest vs 984k for AI Economist.

slides.title: My LLM fishers: the expected fine decides
slides.caption: Measured (L4, Fishery, 20 rounds): 4 gpt-oss-120b fishers and 2 rule-followers, random audits; 10–20 populations per cell, first plays only. Hatched cells were not run.
slides.takeaway: Checking 1 in 12 fishers with a 36 t fine deterred as well as checking 1 in 3 with a 9 t fine.
slides.notes: Every number is from notes/claude_audit_20261005/runs/claude_l4_v1/l4_summary_firstplay.json (overtake_rate, below_half). At an expected fine of 3 t the three audit rates give 9.3%, 9.2% and 10.9% over-taking. At 2 t a rare audit with a big fine deterred more (27.9%) than a frequent small one (40.6%). Announcing audits with a zero fine raised over-taking from 30.2% to 57.5% (finding F4). Over-taking stops between 24 and 30 t, the fine predicted in advance. This is one model; the q comparison ran for gpt-oss only. These checks are random, and 1 in 12 to 1 in 3 is 8-35% of agent-rounds, far above AI-control budgets of 0.5-2% (F9).

slides.title: Fines flip large groups; the rate barely matters
slides.caption: Measured (R1a): Willis et al.'s commons, LLM-written strategies copied by payoff, 20 runs per cell. The 25% rows and the 0.75× and 1.5× columns go beyond the pre-registered grid.

blocks.head: What I measured
blocks.text: In groups of 64, Collective strategies rise from 0.15 to 0.60 at 1.25× a fine predicted before any run. Welfare goes from 0.13 to 0.57.

blocks.head: What it does not test
bullets: Audits are random: nobody chooses whom to check
10–25% of agents checked; AI control uses 0.5–2%

blocks.head: Planned, no data yet
blocks.text: SocialJax Harvest: check k of 7 learning agents per step, swept over k × consequence.

slides.notes: Numbers from notes/claude_audit_20261005/runs/claude_r1a_v1/r1a_conditions.csv (collective_frequency, efficiency_transfer). Strategies are blind to audits, so the effect is selection, not deterrence; equal results at 10% and 25% for the same expected fine are expected for blind strategies. R1b (audit-aware strategies) is the in-game version: Selfish defection falls from 0.74 to 0.06 at an expected fine of 2. The planned SocialJax heatmap uses the same axes as these two slides, but with a budget k of 7 and learning agents.

slides.title: The gap and the first study

items.head: The gap
items.text: MARL interveners see every agent; budgeted-monitoring work has no learning agents in a social dilemma. Nobody tests an overseer that picks k of N agents against learners that adapt.

items.head: First study
items.text: A SocialJax Harvest wrapper: the overseer checks k of 7 agents per step, switched on after the team has learned to over-harvest (Casheekar's "recovery").

items.head: What I'll measure
items.text: Over-harvesting missed and normal harvesting wrongly stopped, as a heatmap over budget k and consequence size (Leibo's Figure 4 style).

items.head: Still to read
items.text: AI Control (Greenblatt), Norm Enforcement (Ye), Blindfold (Zhu), IQ-Flow, Vinitsky sanctions, Green Security Games.

slides.title: Questions for you
questions: Is "whom to check, against agents that evade" a strong enough gap, given Casheekar?
Harvest first, or Clean Up as well?
Learning agents only, or also LLM agents (OpenSocialJax)?
Is there GPU credit for SocialJax training runs?
